usCourseworkText: Note: This School has progressed to a competency-based admissions process.
additionalCoursework:
Drexel moved from a premedical requirements model to competency-based recommendations. Drexel has developed a set of coursework competencies that an applicant's classes may fulfill. Drexel will no longer require specific coursework; however, we want applicants to demonstrate competency in certain key areas.

The premedical curriculum should include significant academic rigor to demonstrate that the applicant can handle the scholastic demands of medical school. The curriculum in medical education necessitates that a student be able to balance a course load that is heavily weighted in the sciences. Taking multiple science courses at the same time and taking as many upper level science courses as possible is valued. 

At least one year of a lab experience in biology, chemistry, or physics is recommended.  The lab experience should have a focus on hypothesis-driven exercises, problem solving, and basic laboratory principles. Additional laboratory and research experiences are valued.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Office of Community Health and Inclusive Excellence supports several student groups including:  Student National Medical Association, Latino Medical Student Association, Drexel Black Doctors Network, LGBT Medical Student Group, and the Drexel Mentoring and Pipeline Program (DMAPP).  The Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences and Professional Studies provides additional support for its students through the Graduate Minority Association and several other Graduate School resources.  All College of Medicine students can also take advantage of University-wide initiatives including:  the Student Center for Inclusion and Culture, LGBTQA+ Student Center and Spiritual and Religious Life.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Requests for a leave of absence are made to the Associate Dean for Student Affairs or the year appropriate Student Promotions committee and may be initiated for one of several reasons; academic, medical, personal, and administrative. Students requesting a leave of absence must submit a written request including the reasons for, the starting date of the leave of absence and probable time of re-entry. A leave of absence may be granted for a period not exceeding one academic year. The Associate Dean for Student Affairs presents the names of students returning from leaves of absence to the year-appropriate Student Promotions Committee.  If that committee mandated certain requirements be met for re-entry, documentation that a student has met those requirements must be submitted. If the committee mandated the leave, it must give approval for the student's return. Tuition, financial aid, and loan repayment may be affected by a leave of absence. medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Every student, regardless of campus, becomes a member of the Student Government Association, which coordinates student activities and provides opportunities for students to express their ideas and make recommendations to faculty and administration. Students are well represented through elected class officers, representatives to student organizations, and student members of medical school committees. The College of Medicine is replete with organizations and discipline-specific interest groups that add to students' academic life. Student organizations include community outreach groups, medical student association groups, Drexel fitness programs, medical student cultural and lifestyle clubs, literary and musical organizations.  Learning communities; Societies; complement the student life experience.  Each student is assigned to a Society which provide a framework for the development of longitudinal relationships among students and between students and faculty.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Philadelphia campus of Drexel University College of Medicine is located in University City. This new facility, the Health Sciences Building (HSB), opened for 1st and 2nd year medical students in August 2023. Drexel University College of Medicine at Tower Health opened a four-year campus in West Reading, PA and began training medical students. This new campus welcomed a third class of 40 first-year students in August 2023 who joined the current 2nd, 3rd and 4th year students. Students at this campus will complete their clinical rotations at Reading Hospital.  The Philadelphia site will continue to house the education facility which is home to the first and second year of medical education for all students not at the Tower Health Reading site.  Both sites feature simulation centers, a student activities center and lounge areas in addition to multiple small group and large group spaces.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is not available. However, resources are available to help students find off-campus housing. The average rent per month is $750 to $1,800 per month.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: DUCOM celebrates the richness of diversity and continues to create and maintain a safe, empowering space for all members of our community including our LGBTQA+ staff, faculty, and students. We understand that for many LGBTQA+ patients, interacting with the medical system is fraught with mistrust, discrimination and trauma. In addition to creating an inclusive environment, we are also dedicated to educating well-rounded, fully competent physicians, equipped to provide compassionate, comprehensive care to their LGBTQA+ patients. Through collaboration with our student groups, we’ve expanded our medical curriculum to include education on taking inclusive, comprehensive gender identity and sexual health histories, and we have small group learning sessions dedicated to practicing these skills and learning more about caring for LQBTQA+ patients. Additionally, the LGBTQA+ Professionals in Medicine group holds an annual LGBTQA+ health symposium, and the pediatric OSCE has a transgender patient.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Drexel University College of Medicine believes wellness is not the mere absence of disease, but an active approach to achieving optimum levels of health that includes physical, emotional, social and spiritual well-being.  Wellness topics are included in the formal curriculum and supported by the Wellness Program workshops and seminars that provide information and active opportunities in developing healthy habits and lifestyles. Students can take an active role in creating wellness programs and events for the student body by serving as wellness representatives for their learning societies.  To help students achieve optimum health, the College of Medicine provides on-campus fitness centers, recreational facilities, relaxation events and professional counseling.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: At Drexel University College of Medicine (DUCOM), we pride ourselves on our vibrant, collaborative, and community oriented culture. Our dynamic, supportive environment is one in which academic achievement and camaraderie go hand in hand. For our students, applauding each other’s successes is as important as celebrating personal milestones. Education at Drexel extends beyond the classroom, offering students numerous opportunities to engage in diverse student groups, social events, and the rich cultures of our surrounding communities. With a focus on individual patient engagement and a commitment to community health, DUCOM cultivates compassionate professionals dedicated to lifelong broad and meaningful impact. This blend of support, service, and collaboration makes Drexel an extraordinary place to become a physician.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: A vehicle is required in years 3 and 4.
medSchoolStudLife.additionalSupportProgrameName: The Office of Career Advising provides career counseling to help students plan their medical school years and beyond with counseling also through the Pathway program.

medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Student Affairs supports student needs and activities from matriculation to career planning and graduation. The Wellness Program provides academic and personal counseling to all students.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Case and team based learning supplemented by self-directed learning through asynchronous lectures.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Longitudinal experience in the preclinical years with a combination of traditional hospital and ambulatory clerkships.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: There is no lecture attendance policy.  However, attendance at live small group activities is required.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
In August 2017, Drexel implemented a new curriculum called Foundations and Frontiers. This program is designed to create physicians for the 21st century who possess the qualities essential to clinical excellence, while also possessing the emerging competencies including an understanding of population health, health informatics, quality and patient safety, and health care systems and financing. The curriculum is organized into three phases: Foundations, Applications and Transitions. Community and civic engagement, technology enhanced instructional formats and learning as a member of a team are key.

More information is found on Drexel's website at http://drexel.edu/medicine/academics/md-program/curriculum/.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Because of the importance of research in undergraduate medical education, the College of Medicine has established the Office of Research for Medical Students. A variety of opportunities are available to students who are interested in doing research while in medical school, including a summer research program and research during the academic year. Students can arrange to take a year off through the EDGE (Educational Development Growth Experiences) program to conduct research at Drexel or away. We also have a two-week fourth year elective in translational research. While conducting research is not a requirement of the general MD curriculum (unless you're a student in the MD/PhD program), over 50% of our students feel that it's an important part of their learning process and involve themselves voluntarily in the research, both on-campus and off.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: The Health Advocacy Program is a core course in the first and second years which is focused on learning about social determinants of health, health disparities, and trauma responsive care.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Drexel University College of Medicine was formed when two historic Philadelphia medical schools joined their rich histories and resources. The Medical College of Pennsylvania (MCP) was founded in 1850 as the first medical school for women. Hahnemann University, a private nondenominational institution, was founded in 1848. Drexel offers a medical education rich in history and diversity, while providing the foundational curriculum and learning environment necessary for the scientific, technological, and ethical decisions required of physicians in the 21st century.  Continuing its growth and forward thinking, Drexel has opened two new campuses over the last few years and now has a new building  in University City (Philadelphia) and another in West Reading, PA.  Students at both campuses have the same outstanding curriculum, mentoring by expert faculty, and are given opportunities to pursue passions through exposure to diverse and underserved communities.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Drexel University College of Medicine delivers innovative biomedical education in an environment that embraces inquiry and collaboration, founded on excellence in patient care, and based on a culture of, and respect for diversity. These principles are built upon the College's legacy of a firm commitment to meeting the healthcare needs of the communities in which we live and work.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: Drexel University College of Medicine has a BA/BS + MD Early Assurance Program for undergraduate students enrolled at Drexel University. This 4 + 4 combined degree program is designed to provide outstanding high school students who are highly motivated toward the medical profession the opportunity to gain provisional early acceptance to Drexel University College of Medicine. During their undergraduate career, combined-degree students will also participate in the Drexel Co-op program where students pursue six months of professional employment related to their field of study. This unique feature distinguishes this BA/BS + MD Early Assurance Program from others in the nation.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: The College of Medicine requires letters of recommendation. We prefer a committee letter if your school has one, but we also accept letters from up to four individuals who can provide objective evaluations and with whom the applicant has had a recent professional relationship.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Drexel is using the MMI process and holding group interviews with a student which are closed file.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: MMI interview and group interview with student-closed-file
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: All applicants who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents.  Permanent residents are required to provide the Admissions Office with a copy of their valid green card.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Only U.S. citizens or permanent residents may apply.  Permanent residents are required to provide the Admissions Office with a copy of their valid green card.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: U.S. Citizens and Permanent residents from any state are welcomed.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Please see more information about Drexel College of Medicine at https://drexel.edu/medicine/academics/md-program/md-program-admissions/
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo:
Drexel University will accept scores through September 2026 for the 2027 application year. January 2027 scores are not considered for applicants applying for the 2027 entering class unless they are in an early assurance or bachelors/MD programs.

We review all MCAT scores, but are especially interested in the most recent. We do not consider "best of" scores, but look at the scores from each exam.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Regardless of the undergraduate GPA, we always consider post baccalaureate and/or graduate grades.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: Regardless of the undergraduate GPA, we always consider post baccalaureate and/or graduate grades and credit hours.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We will review community college coursework on an individual basis through our holistic review process.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Drexel accepts letters of intent and interest as well as updates.  Transcripts are also accepted if an applicant has new grades to provide.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: The goal of Drexel University College of Medicine is to prepare our medical graduates to be competent, caring physicians who have the skills of lifelong learning necessary to incorporate new knowledge and methods into their practice as either a generalist or a specialist and to adapt to a changing professional environment. Essential abilities and characteristics required for completion of the MD degree consist of certain minimum physical and cognitive abilities and sufficient mental and emotional stability to assure that candidates for admission, promotion, and graduation are able to complete the entire course of study and participate fully in all aspects of medical training. Drexel intends for its graduates to become physicians who are capable of pursuing and completing graduate medical education, passing licensing exams and obtaining and maintaining medical licensure.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: In addition to the Federal Direct Student Loan Program, the Primary Care Loan Program, other federally funded programs, and assistance in obtaining money from foundation sources, Drexel also has limited private scholarship and loan funds that are awarded to students based on financial need. Work-Study for qualified students is also available.  Secondary application fee waivers are granted if approved by AMCAS.  To help students manage their entire financial picture beyond financial aid, Drexel has a full-time financial planner on staff and available to all students and alumni.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: The Drexel College of Medicine financial planning program is designed to assist students whose resources are insufficient to meet their educational costs.  Awards are based on financial need.  Some scholarship monies may be awarded each year on a competitive basis to academically outstanding incoming first-year medical students who possess an undergraduate degree and show qualities of leadership, humanity and community service.  Additional scholarship may be awarded each year to students based on need or on academic performance during the preceding medical school year. Students are encouraged to make an appointment to see one of the financial aid officers or the financial planner if they need assistance in managing a budget or personal cash flow.  In addition, educational seminars are offered periodically to students and house staff on debt management and financial planning issues.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The MD/PhD program will only accept applications from Drexel's matriculated MD class as transfer students into the MD/PhD program. No external application for direct entry into the MD/PhD program will be accepted. MD applicants interested in this internal-only program should select the MD/PhD option on the secondary application.

Current second- and third-year Drexel MD students who are interested in completing an MD/PhD degree are invited to apply. These students will join the MD/PhD program in the fall after completing their third year as first year PhD students. Students will complete their PhD training before returning for their last year of medical school.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Applicants must adhere to all AAMC acceptance protocols and update their Choose Your Medical School Tool in a timely manner.
If accepted after April 30:  Applicants must select either Plan to Enroll or Commit to Enroll in the Choose your Medical School Tool from AMCAS no later than two (2) weeks after acceptance.
If accepted on or before April 30:  Applicants should select Plan to Enroll in the Choose your Medical School Tool from AMCAS if they have determined a first-choice medical school

On or before the last Monday in June:   Applicants must select the Commit to Enroll option in the Choose Your Medical School Tool from AMCAS.  Applicants must withdraw all applications from other medical schools.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The waitlist is ranked by the Admissions Committee.  If applicants are taken from the waitlist, they are called/emailed and asked to reply ASAP.  Waitlisted applicants may send up three updates.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: In order to fulfill the basic requirements for matriculation at Drexel College of Medicine, we have for many years required a specific set of courses. In recent years, however, the scientific knowledge important to the learning and practice of medicine has changed and expanded dramatically.  The AAMC in conjunction with the Howard Hughes Medical Institute updated its recommendations for premedical learning and included both scientific and personal competencies.   Drexel recognizes that these scientific and personal competencies are important to the study and practice of medicine in the 21st century.  We have, therefore, modified and updated the premedical coursework and experiences we would like our students to have experienced.  Please review our MD Program Admissions Requirements page for more information on our recommendations.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Considered on a case by case basis.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Drexel seeks highly qualified, motivated students who demonstrate the desire, intelligence, integrity, and emotional maturity to become excellent physicians. We encourage nontraditional applicants and are committed to a diverse student body.  Our admissions committee utilizes the process of Holistic Review in the consideration of applicants to the College of Medicine.  Our committee also values students who have overcome personal, economic or educational hardship, students who are first generation college graduates, and students who have demonstrated commitment to community service and leadership.  The committee has a positive attitude toward students who have had varied experiences and are interested in medicine as a second career. We seek students who have a firm grasp of the biological and physical sciences as well as broad educational experiences in other areas, regardless of the field of study.  Students who demonstrate a commitment to community service are strongly considered.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Our committee values students who have demonstrated a commitment to community service and leadership and have experience and/or exposure to the field of medicine.
